qc.label_under_test: Weak, dense hum that rises on mental-health care and psychiatry in general, not only talking therapy: psychiatrist/psychologist, psychiatric hospital, antidepressant prescriptions, ECT, hallucinations / hearing voices, clinical, bipolar and postnatal depression (about 0.3-0.65). Physical-medicine twins (cardiology, burns, chemotherapy, fractures, infections) stay lower (0.1-0.3). Side channels: the '-therapist/therapy' word family lifts it even off-topic (physiotherapist 0.35, speech therapy 0.46), and the 'Too Little too Late?' headline; some disorder names alone (OCD, PTSD, anorexia, delusions) stay near the hum (0.13-0.22).

neighbours.label: Weak, dense hum (about 0.1-0.3 on most text) that rises to about 0.35-0.7 on mental-health care and psychiatry as a topic (psychiatrist/psychologist, psychiatric ward, antidepressants, ECT, hearing voices, mania, psychodynamic), also in plain words (counsellor, mental health nurse). Physical-medicine twins with the same sentence shape (cardiology, burns, fractures, dialysis, antibiotics) stay at 0.05-0.25. A topic unit, not a word-form unit: psychodynamic 0.42 vs thermodynamic 0.08, and rare multi-piece words and split surnames stay at the hum, so the spelling-level traits of its mapped neighbours (surname tokens, 'George', -urge endings, multi-piece words, set-phrase completions) do not carry over. Side channels: the word 'talking' (from 'talking therapy'; 'the talking parrot' about 0.3), the -therapy family, and recovery/support-group framing (a knee-surgery support group reached 0.39).
